sections.h2: Offices behind the Georgetown tax bill
sections.html:
Georgetown sits in Williamson County, so two county-level offices touch every bill. One office sets value and another collects. The Williamson Central Appraisal District appraises each parcel and handles exemptions, while the Williamson County Tax Office takes payment for the city, the county and other contracting units.

Mail and payments go to 1848 Texas Trail, Georgetown, TX 78626, and the phone is (512) 943-1601. The office accepts cash, checks, money orders and cards. Cards add a 2.15 percent convenience fee (minimum $2.50), and online e-checks carry no vendor fee.

The county also runs a tax transparency site at williamsonpropertytaxes.org, which shows the taxing units on a parcel and the dates of public hearings where rates are set. Taxing units set exemptions and rates. Neither the appraisal district nor the tax office does.

The Georgetown levy for 2026 is $0.363167 for each $100 of taxable value, compared with $0.353000 the year before. The city's notice of public hearing printed that figure as both the proposed rate and the voter-approval rate, with a no-new-revenue rate of $0.362168.

The average homestead taxable value went from $404,662 in 2025 to $390,088 in 2026, and the city's total levy on all properties went from $51,935,169 to $53,967,701. The city held its hearing on August 25, 2026 in Council Chambers at 510 W 9th Street.

This is the city's slice only. Williamson County, the school district that serves your street and any municipal utility or special district add their own rates. County statements for 2026 were planned to go out the week of October 19.

Pay by January 31 to avoid delinquency, which begins February 1. A unit may give at least 21 days after mailing, which means a bill mailed after January 10 can push delinquency to the first of a later month.

The collector charges 6 percent in penalty plus 1 percent in interest starting February 1. Each following month the penalty gains a point until it stands at 12 percent in July, and interest never stops. A collection attorney's fee, capped at 20 percent, can be added by a unit that hires one.

Calendar for a Georgetown homeowner
WhenWhat to expect
Jan. 1The parcel is valued and the year's lien attaches
About Apr. 1Single-family homestead owners get a notice of appraised value
Apr. 30Last day of the regular homestead filing period
May 15Protest filing deadline, or 30 days after delivery if later
Nov. 30First installment when the bill is paid in two halves
Jan. 31Final day to pay; unpaid balances turn delinquent Feb. 1
June 30Second half of a split bill

Owners who are seniors, have disabilities or are disabled-veteran owners may pay in four parts. Owners who fall behind may ask the collector about a plan. Some offices stretch these to 36 months.

Begin with a residence homestead application with the Williamson Central Appraisal District. The regular window is January 1 to April 30. Miss it and a late application is still taken for two years after taxes go delinquent. An approved exemption renews on its own unless you move or the chief appraiser requests a new form.

  • The online route runs through the district's property search: find the parcel, then click the HS Exemption icon. Paper applications are accepted too.
  • The senior exemption starts in the year an owner turns 65.
  • Homestead land is limited to what the owner keeps for residential use, up to 20 acres, and generally an acre or less.
  • For disabled-veteran owners the rating must be 10 percent or higher. At 100 percent, or with 100 percent unemployability pay, the homestead exemption can be total.
  • A surviving spouse who is 55 or older can take over the school tax ceiling of an owner who held the over-65 exemption.

School taxes are figured on $140,000 less value, and $60,000 less again for owners 65 or older or disabled. A homestead's appraised value rises no more than 10 percent a year, beginning the year after the exemption is first granted. Think the value is too high? Protest by May 15, or 30 days after a late notice is delivered.

Georgetown has grown fast. The July 2025 estimate of 106,907 residents sits 58.5 percent over the 67,436 estimate base from April 2020, and the 2010 count was 47,400. Land area is 57.33 square miles, and owners live in 69.5 percent of homes. Middle home value is $429,100 and middle monthly rent is $1,795 for 2020 to 2024. About 26.2 percent of residents are past 65, the age that opens the senior exemptions and the school tax ceiling.

sections.h2: Preparing a Georgetown house for sale
sections.html:
Having tax records in order keeps your closing date from slipping over a missing document.

Sort the tax paperwork before you list. Pull your latest statement from the county tax office at (512) 943-1601, confirm which exemptions the appraisal district has on file, and write down any unpaid year. Buyers and title officers ask for these first.

If the house is inherited, collect the death certificate, a utility bill and a sworn statement of interest from each heir. If it is a rental or sits vacant, plan on the full rate, since no homestead relief applies. A cash sale does not change what is owed, but it can close fast enough that the payoff figure needs to be ready on day one.

sections.h2: Can I sell while behind on taxes?
sections.html:
Yes. At closing, the escrow officer pays the overdue balance from the seller's funds. Request a full payoff statement from the county tax office, current year included, because the lien attached on January 1 to whoever owned the house then.

If the February deadline is near or the penalty months have begun, a short payment agreement can limit the damage. Waiving penalty and interest is possible on a written request, filed before the 181st day after delinquency and usually once the tax itself is paid.

  • Heirs who want the homestead on an inherited house hand the district three things: a sworn statement of ownership interest, the prior owner's death certificate and a utility bill.
  • Rentals and vacant properties receive no homestead relief, so the full rate applies.
  • A house in poor repair with a tax lien can still sell, with the lien paid at closing.

faqs.q: What is Georgetown's 2026 city tax rate?
faqs.a: $0.363167 per $100 of taxable value, up from $0.353000 in 2025. Your school district, the county and any special district charge separate rates on top.

faqs.q: How do I pay the Georgetown tax bill?
faqs.a: Payments go to the Williamson County Tax Office at 1848 Texas Trail, Georgetown, TX 78626, whether online or by mail. Cards add a 2.15 percent fee with a $2.50 minimum, while e-checks avoid the vendor fee.

faqs.q: Until when can I file a Georgetown homestead application?
faqs.a: April 30 closes the regular filing period. Late applications are accepted for two years after taxes go delinquent.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss January 31?
faqs.a: From February 1 a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest apply. The penalty grows a point each month through July, and interest continues to build.

faqs.q: Can heirs get a homestead exemption on an inherited Georgetown house?
faqs.a: Yes, when the heir lives there as a principal residence. An heir missing from the recorded deed supplies a sworn statement of interest, the death certificate and a utility bill.
